text: In Frank Jackson's knowledge argument, Mary knows every physical fact about color vision from inside a black-and-white room. What is the argument's route to the conclusion that physicalism is false?
choices: Mental types can be realized by different neural states in different creatures, so mental types are not physical types.
On first seeing red Mary learns something new, namely what it is like to see red, so she did not already know all the facts and some facts are non-physical.
A physical duplicate of Mary who entirely lacks phenomenal consciousness is conceivable, and therefore metaphysically possible.
Talk of 'seeing red' belongs to folk psychology, which a mature neuroscience will ultimately eliminate.
explanation: The knowledge argument turns on an epistemic premise: complete physical knowledge omits knowledge of what experience is like, so not every fact is physical. Option 0 is the multiple realizability argument (which targets type-identity, not physicalism as such), option 2 is the separate zombie/conceivability argument, and option 3 is eliminativism. Each is a real position in the debate, but none is Jackson's line of reasoning.
